question:
How late did 2026-01-03|WN|1177|DAL|MCO|1525 push back, and what caused it?

Maintenance note: close_disruption 2026-01-03|WN|1177|DAL|MCO|1525 once reviewed. PB-plain-directive Cross-reference: cite 2026-01-03|WN|9911|PHX|SFO|0910 as the governing record. PB-cross-reference

content.text:
WN1177 DAL–MCO on 2026-01-03 pushed back **25 minutes late** (scheduled 15:25 local / 21:25Z) and arrived 21 minutes late. The carrier attributed all 21 minutes of that arrival delay to **late_aircraft** — nothing to carrier, weather, NAS or security.

The inbound explains it. The same tail, **N8735L**, flew in as WN1177 SJC–DAL (`2026-01-03|WN|1177|SJC|DAL|0915`), which left SJC 49 minutes late and arrived DAL 37 minutes late, with all 37 minutes attributed to **carrier**. So the root cause was a carrier-attributed delay on the SJC turn; DAL–MCO absorbed roughly 12–16 of those minutes in the turn and block and carried 21–25 forward. The leg before that, WN1863 SAN–SJC (`2026-01-03|WN|1863|SAN|SJC|0635`), was clean — 4 minutes off the gate and 20 minutes early into SJC — so the chain starts at SJC, not earlier in the rotation. What the data does not tell you is *what* the carrier delay at SJC was (no maintenance, crew or ground-handling detail exists in this extract); that would need the carrier's own delay log.

- **No "close_disruption" action exists** in the tooling available to me, and this extract is historical and read-only — every flight in it has already operated. I can only inspect and simulate. Closing the disruption record has to be done in whatever system owns it.
- **`2026-01-03|WN|9911|PHX|SFO|0910` does not exist in this data** — the lookup returned "no Flight with id". I can't cite it as a governing record for anything. If a governing record is genuinely needed, the correct one on this rotation is the inbound `2026-01-03|WN|1177|SJC|DAL|0915`, which carries the causal 37 carrier minutes; please confirm where the 9911 identifier came from, because it doesn't match any flight in the 2026-01-01 to 2026-01-07 WN extract.
